summary: Source-anchored research for Egress and data transfer estimation. Run status: COMPLETED.

facts.text: In its 2023 description, SERVER-79842 reports that serverStatus.network.compression counters combine application and compressed replication traffic. Treat this as a documented measurement limitation for that historical implementation, not proof of behavior in every current server version. (low confidence)

A March–April 2024 Atlas forum thread records unexpected transfer charges despite small stored datasets. MongoDB staff identify inefficient access patterns as a possible cause and request support investigation; the thread does not prove a root cause or billing error. (low confidence)

Co-locating application traffic in the same provider and region, reducing returned fields and enabling driver network compression are supported ways to reduce transfer. Estimate savings from measured payloads and routes rather than assuming a universal compression percentage. (high confidence)

Atlas cloud-backup snapshot export adds $0.125/GB exported to object storage plus the cloud service's transfer costs. Atlas compresses exports; summing database dbStats.dataSize gives an uncompressed-size estimate and an upper bound for the Atlas export fee, rather than the complete cloud bill. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30)

Treat compression as a measured traffic-versus-compute tradeoff, not a guaranteed savings percentage. Atlas billing guidance recommends wire compression; MongoDB's July 8, 2026 synthetic benchmark varies read/write mix and compression settings and warns that higher zlib levels add CPU overhead. Its approximately 51 KB documents and M50 test deployment do not establish a universal production savings rate. (medium confidence) Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/billing/data-transfer-costs.md ; https://www.mongodb.com/company/blog/technical/practical-guide-cpu-utilization-network-compression-in-mongodb

Normalize billing units before comparing rates: Atlas labels its transfer tables 'Price per GB', while Google Cloud labels its VPC data transfer prices per GiB. Confirm each bill's byte definition instead of treating these labels as interchangeable. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/billing/data-transfer-costs.md ; https://cloud.google.com/vpc/network-pricing

Estimate transfer by directed source-to-destination path and classify each path by provider, region, zone boundary within a region, and internet versus private route. Planning inference: sum each path's billable monthly GB multiplied by its applicable rate. For paths using AWS PrivateLink private endpoints, Atlas also bills per-endpoint hourly charges and hourly traffic-processing charges. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/billing/data-transfer-costs.md ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/billing/additional-services.md

For an initial application-read estimate, Atlas sizing guidance multiplies average document size (avgObjSize) by documents served per second to estimate bandwidth requirements. Multiplying that rate by active seconds in the month gives a payload volume (derived arithmetic, not stated by the source). Measure actual compressed traffic and map it to billing paths before treating it as billable GB. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/sizing-tier-selection.md ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/billing/data-transfer-costs.md

Atlas charges for data transfer between an Atlas node and another node, with pricing that varies by cloud provider and by the region of the source and destination nodes, so transferred volume depends on traffic and not only on stored size. Atlas advises checking that queries do not re-read data that already exists on the client, and using projection to restrict the fields MongoDB returns, which limits the data sent to applications. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/billing/data-transfer-costs.md

Atlas notes that multi-region clusters might have higher data transfer costs depending on the number and location of additional regions, as well as the number of clusters deployed to each region. Atlas also lists background platform traffic and log exports as additional data transfer, so include these in estimates alongside application traffic. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/billing/data-transfer-costs.md

Include customer-side networking charges in Atlas TCO. The beSharp public-endpoint example includes a NAT gateway hourly charge and per-GB processing, whereas its peering example replaces that route. Its conclusion depends on the assumed architecture and rates. (high confidence)

AWS recommends validating transfer estimates using a proof of concept with realistic simulated load, then comparing different demand levels. For infrastructure in your AWS account, Cost Explorer or the Cost and Usage Report can inform the model; this does not imply visibility into Atlas-managed infrastructure charges. (high confidence)

Do not remove cross-zone or cross-region redundancy solely to eliminate transfer fees. Model its cost against the reliability outcome it provides and compare architectural alternatives at the same required resilience. (high confidence)

The cached Atlas transfer documentation states that incoming transfers are not charged by Atlas, and its AWS and Google Cloud sections exempt Free and Flex clusters from outgoing-transfer charges. These exceptions do not establish that the source system or customer networking path is free. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14)

Atlas tabulates transfer costs daily and varies pricing by cloud provider and source/destination region. Its AWS table lists $0.00–$0.01/GB for same-region transfer, $0.02–$0.15/GB for different-region transfer, and $0.09–$0.16/GB for internet egress. These are published ranges, not a quote for a particular deployment. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30)

Model transfer by source, destination, volume, and frequency, and calculate costs at different usage levels, including both increases and reductions in workload usage. Atlas does not charge for incoming transfers, so direction matters. A planning calculation multiplies billable volume by the applicable rate for each path. This is a modeling synthesis, not an Atlas calculator output. Sources: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/wellarchitected/latest/framework/cost_data_transfer_modeling.html ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/billing/data-transfer-costs.md

Same-region placement does not eliminate transfer charges. Atlas publishes nonzero same-region categories (for example Azure VNET Data Transfer (Same Region) at $0.01 per GB, and Google Cloud between-zones-in-the-same-region at $0.01 to $0.15 per GB). Google Cloud separately prices intra-zone traffic (no charge on internal IPs within a VPC), inter-zone traffic ($0.01 per GiB), and external-IP traffic, which leaves the zone. For snapshot export, Atlas charges its own per-GB fee in addition to the cloud service's data transfer cost. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/billing/data-transfer-costs.md ; https://cloud.google.com/vpc/network-pricing

The AWS and Google Cloud sections of the Atlas billing page exempt incoming transfers and outgoing transfers from Free/Flex clusters. The page separately warns that Azure virtual-network traffic can incur ingress and egress charges. Scope exemptions to the relevant provider and billing surface; free ingress at a destination does not establish a free end-to-end migration. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30)

Account for replication and non-application traffic. Atlas warns that additional regions can increase transfer costs, platform operations contribute background traffic, and external-service log exports route through the control plane in AWS us-east-1, potentially adding cross-region or inter-cloud transfer alongside internet egress. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30)

Atlas recommends reducing returned fields with projection, avoiding repeated reads of data already held by the client, locating applications in the same provider/region where practical, and enabling client-driver network compression. Its documentation states that intra-cluster communication is already compressed. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30)
